page: Amazon Web Services g5.48xlarge is an accelerated computing instance built on the AWS Nitro System, engineered for distributed graphics rendering and machine learning inference. It is driven by an AMD EPYC 7R32 processor providing 96 physical cores and 192 dedicated vCPUs operating at a 3.3 GHz clock frequency on the x86_64 architecture. The system configuration includes 768.0 GB of DDR4 memory clocked at 3 GHz, balancing out to 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware acceleration is delivered via eight discrete NVIDIA Ampere A10G GPUs with an aggregate total of 179 GB of GPU VRAM. Storage consists of 7,600 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD capacity, supported by a baseline network throughput of 100 Gbps.

Benchmark data reflects top-tier scaling across multi-GPU and parallel computing operations. In machine learning evaluations, the instance demonstrates top 10% inference execution for prompt processing across small, medium, and 70B parameter models, reaching 393.89 tokens per second on 70B models and 8,898.3 tokens per second on smaller 135M architectures. Parallel computing metrics confirm this scale, with a PassMark CPU score of 94,547.15 and Geekbench ray tracing scoring 109,948.0, both placing within the top decile. In contrast, single-thread performance is a limiting factor: the stress-ng single-core score of 753.2 falls into the bottom 10%, indicating that tasks bound to individual thread frequency rather than parallelism will experience performance bottlenecks.

From an efficiency standpoint, the consolidation of eight GPUs, substantial NVMe capacity, and 100 Gbps networking provides high resource density for workloads requiring co-located compute and low-latency storage. The memory architecture delivers 156.19 million operations per second in Redis SET operations and strong static web serving throughput of 46.87 GB/sec. However, the hardware footprint is cost-inefficient for single-threaded tasks or applications that cannot evenly partition workloads across all eight A10G GPUs. Best-fit use cases include multi-GPU large language model inference serving, high-throughput video encoding, distributed rendering pipelines, and parallelized scientific simulations.
description: Amazon Web Services g5.48xlarge is a high-density accelerated computing instance designed for distributed graphics and machine learning inference. Built on the AWS Nitro System, it features 192 dedicated vCPUs across 96 physical cores powered by an AMD EPYC 7R32 processor running at 3.3 GHz. The hardware architecture integrates 768.0 GB of DDR4 memory, 7,600 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, and eight NVIDIA Ampere A10G GPUs supplying 179 GB of total VRAM, with 100 Gbps baseline networking. Benchmark evaluations indicate top-tier capabilities in large language model inference, parallel compilation, and ray tracing, alongside 156.19 million Redis operations per second. While single-thread CPU benchmarks fall into the lowest decile, the instance delivers balanced multi-GPU density and memory bandwidth for distributed AI serving, ray-traced graphics rendering, and intensive batch processing pipelines.
